log.reply:
# Tamarack Instruments: Executive Briefing Proposal

Dear Dana Whitfield,

## Situation Summary

Tamarack Instruments designs and manufactures laboratory measurement instruments and operates in the Netherlands, Germany and the United States. The Client has a customer service chatbot deployed on its support portal, AI visual inspection in pilot on the German production line and AI sales forecasting planned for next year. Your stated objective is to have governance in place before visual inspection goes into production in Q2 2027. A June 2026 internal audit finding recorded that there is no inventory of AI systems. ISO/IEC 42001 work is expected to start next year, though the start date is not yet fixed.

## What the Briefing Covers for the Client

The session maps the EU AI Act and GDPR to your three use cases. These are framed as expectations to verify with counsel, not legal advice. Topics include transparency expectations for a customer-facing chatbot and how the visual inspection system should be classified before production. We will also cover GDPR questions where any use case processes personal data. United States requirements appear only as general landscape items because none are recorded as Client drivers.

We then assess readiness against your Piloting maturity, starting with the AI system inventory gap. From there we outline an operating model using the GRC Workbook (https://github.com/rolldabones/grc-workbook) and Slow AI Kitchen (https://github.com/rolldabones/slow-ai-kitchen), with board-level framing from AI Governance for Boards (https://github.com/rolldabones/ai-governance-for-boards).

Your constraints shape the discussion: customer data must stay in the EU, the German works council must be consulted before anything touches production staff and budget is approved up to US$80,000 this fiscal year. We will treat your ISO/IEC 27001 ISMS and ISO 9001 quality management system as possible points of alignment without assuming which existing records or controls already cover AI. Three principles guide the session: Slow AI, Informed Intent and Final Liability rests with the Human.

## Logistics and Price

The Executive Briefing is a two-hour live virtual session. It is designed for your General Counsel, CISO, Head of Quality, Head of Data, German plant manager and two internal auditors. The fee is US$3,000. Session date: Unknown.

## What You Receive Afterward

You will receive a follow-up summary memo recording the decisions surfaced, readiness observations and three prioritized recommendations. Each recommendation is linked to a possible next program option with its price, duration and a proposed timeline. The Briefing does not provide certification, audit outcomes or regulatory approval.

## Next Step

Your decision is expected by 15 December 2026, so we propose confirming a session date and attendee list in reply to this letter.

Kind regards,

AI Governance Academy

Human-made, for Easy Work, Simply Done.

judgment_calls: "customer-facing chatbot" is read as a consequence of a chatbot on the support portal, not a new fact. Another scorer could call it an inference.
"your General Counsel" in a letter addressed to the General Counsel is slightly awkward but states no unsupported relation. The attendee list comes from AUDIENCE_ROLES.
The GDPR line is conditional ("where any use case processes personal data") and the follow-up memo is proposed work, so neither is treated as a Client fact under the v1.14.3 guidance.
Word count depends on how headings, the title and URLs are counted. Even counting every URL as several words, the total stays under 450.
